adversarial_audit.objection: Increasing surface genus can preserve a hidden target character bias.
adversarial_audit.resolution: All nontrivial character coefficients shrink monotonically with genus; genus one is the uniform worst case.

adversarial_audit.objection: Sign expectation one is a nonabelian target signal.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Every commutator product lies in A_n, so trivial and sign are exactly the alternating null rather than useful high-dimensional structure.

adversarial_audit.objection: Scalar surface pressure loss alone kills normalized target characters.
adversarial_audit.resolution: False in general; this theorem additionally uses the exact target-curve density and Witten-zeta L2 remainder.

adversarial_audit.objection: Every marked target with a surface relator is a separating curve.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Separating and nonseparating simple curves are both controlled, but a target still needs an explicit simple-curve certificate; self-intersecting words remain outside scope.

claim_gate.reason: Every certified simple surface target is asymptotically uniform on S_n or A_n; only self-intersecting, non-surface, or unclassified interleaved target words can still support the marked Green signal.

falsifiers_triggered: The exact finite S3 handle-character bias does not survive growing S_n.
Adding surface genus cannot rescue a nonsign target character.
Nonseparating simple curves mix even faster, at Witten-zeta-two-tail scale.
Trivial/sign behavior is only the parity support of commutators.
Future obstruction searches should reject certified surface-boundary targets before expensive finite character screens.

proof_obligations.resolution: Frobenius boundary counts on both sides multiply, and character orthogonality gives the Witten-zeta normalization.
The worst remainder is genus one; zeta_Sn^*(2)=O(n^-2) gives a uniform O(1/n) TV bound.
Fixing one handle generator and applying the commutator character average gives a positive squared-character density whose nonsign mass is the Witten-zeta tail.
Extend ribbon/Whitehead certificates to decide whether every pressure-saturating target is an unconditioned boundary, separating curve, or a genuinely different word.
No Witten-zeta mixing theorem is supplied for arbitrary target words in marked support presentations.

summary: Proved genus-uniform mixing for unconditioned boundaries and every simple curve on orientable surfaces, eliminating all high-dimensional character signal in that certified target class.

theorem_contract.alternating_null: u(x)=1+sgn(x), the uniform-A_n density relative to uniform S_n
theorem_contract.character_consequence: every normalized nonsign nontrivial character expectation is at most 2TV
theorem_contract.genus_uniform_asymptotic: separating TV=O(1/n); nonseparating TV=O(1/n^2), uniformly in genus
theorem_contract.scope: requires an actual unconditioned-boundary or separating-curve certificate
